content:
We have list of templates. Need the one that matches our target molecule and corresponds to amide formation from carboxylic acid. The templates list includes retro_smarts_template. We need to apply each to our target molecule to get precursors. Likely the correct template is the one where retro_smarts_template shows amide to acid? Let's examine each:

1st entry: retro_smarts_template: '[#7:2]-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:3])/[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5]>>C-C(-C)(-C)-O-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[#7:2])=[O;D1;H0:3].O-C(=O)-[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5]'

This seems to be a template for amide + alkene to something else? Not sure.

2nd entry: retro_smarts_template: '[#7:5]-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:2])-[C:3]=[C:4]>>O-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:2])-[C:3]=[C:4]'

This is amide to ester? Not our case.

3rd entry similar.

4th entry: retro_smarts_template: '[#7:2]-[C;H0;D3;+0:3](-[C:4])=[O;H0;D1;+0:1]>>O-C(=[O;H0;D1;+0:1])-C-C1=C-C-c2:c:c:c:c:c:2-1.[#7:2]-[CH2;D2;+0:3]-[C:4]'

This seems to break amide to acid plus something else.

5th entry: similar.

We need template that when applied to our target (which contains amide linking a phenyl amine to a carbonyl attached to a conjugated alkene). The amide is -C(=O)N- attached to phenyl. The template likely is amide formation from acid + amine. The retro template would break amide into acid and amine. So we need a template where retro_smarts_template has amide on product side? Actually retro_smarts_template is the retrosynthetic direction: product (target) -> precursors. So it should have amide on left side? Let's check entry 4: retro_smarts_template: '[#7:2]-[C;H0;D3;+0:3](-[C:4])=[O;H0;D1;+0:1]>>O-C(=[O;H0;D1;+0:1])-C-C1=... .[#7:2]-[CH2;D2;+0:3]-[C:4]'

Left side is amide (N-C=O) attached to carbon (C). Right side gives acid (O-C=O) plus amine fragment. That matches.

Thus template ID for entry 4: need template_hash? But we need template ID. The search result didn't give template_id, only template_hash and retro_smarts_template. Possibly template_id is the hash? Might be template_hash. But apply_template expects template_id string. Could be the hash. Let's try applying template using that hash.

We'll use apply_template with target SMILES and template_id = the hash string.
